text:
**For a one-day recharge of a 1000Wh station, plan on about 300 W of solar panel in decent sun. A 200 W panel works too, but it takes about a day and a half.**

**The math**
- Losses (heat, panel angle, charge controller) mean panels deliver roughly 70-80% of their rating. Sources use 0.68-0.8 ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/), [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)).
- Panel watts ≈ 1000 Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.75)

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts for a 1-day recharge |
|---|---|
| 3 (winter, cloudy) | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 (summer, Southwest) | ~230 W |

These come from the [Power Runtime guide](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/). [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/how-many-watts-solar-panel-to-recharge-1000wh-portable-power-station-solar-charg) gives similar numbers: about 200 W at 6 hours, 300 W at 4 hours, and 400 W at 3 hours.

**If you have less panel**
- A 200 W panel on an average day (4.5 sun hours, 70%) gives about 630 Wh, so roughly 1.5 days ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- A quick rule of thumb is battery Wh ÷ 5 ≈ 200 W for about a day and a half.
- In a northern winter, a one-day recharge can take 700 W or more ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**Check these before buying**
1. **Your station's maximum solar input (watts).** Panels above the cap add nothing, though modest oversizing helps in weak light.
2. **The input voltage window.** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay under the station's limit, or it can damage the charge controller. Panels wired in series add voltage.
3. **The connector.** MC4 panels often need an adapter for XT60 or DC ports.
4. **Running loads while charging.** Net charge is solar input minus what you're drawing.

**One example panel**
The ALLPOWERS SP037 is a 400 W foldable panel with a 37.4 V working and 45.3 V open-circuit voltage. It's listed at $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26, which was reported to expire 2026-12-30. It fits stations with 12-60 V solar inputs, such as the BLUETTI AC180 or ALLPOWERS P1800. It does not fit low-voltage inputs like the Tenergy T320 or BLUETTI Elite 30 V2, and at 18.5 kg it's heavy for a folding panel. [Buy the ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric is paid if you buy, at no cost to you.
